newsitem.title: THAILAND: Three dead as clashes on Thai-Burma border worsen.
newsitem.headline: Three dead as clashes on Thai-Burma border worsen.

text.p: Thai troops repelled guerrillas trying to cross over from Burma and reinforced the border area as fighting continued between rival factions of the Karen rebel group, Karen and Thai sources said on Monday.

Thai troops were engaged in heavy mortar exchanges on Sunday with the pro-Rangoon Democratic Karen Buddhist Army (DKBA) when about 100 guerrillas attempted to cross the river to attack refugee camps inside Thailand, a source from the Thai border patrol police said.
Casualty figures were not available but the situation was expected to intensify because the guerrillas have threatened to keep attacking the refugee camps, the police source said.
The Thais have sent heavy reinforcements into the areas, an army source said. Eight armoured personnel carriers and four helicopter gunships were seen patrolling the area, he said.
"The situation is very tense because the DKBA are poised to cross the river to attack the refugees camps from many points," a border patrol police source said.

The refugee official said troops of Burma's 99 Light Infantry Division were based at Manerplaw, the former headquarters of the Karen National Union (KNU), and were ready to cross the river into Thailand to attack the Ma Ra Ma Luang refugee camp.
Separately, three members of a Rangoon-backed ethnic Karen organisation were killed near a refugee camp inside Thailand after being ambushed by refugee guards, Karen sources said.

The three members of the DKBA -- the organisation accused of raiding and torching three refugee camps in Thailand last week -- were killed on Sunday just outside the Mae La refugee camp, a refugee official said in a statement obtained by Reuters on Monday.

The Mae La camp houses about 25,000 Karen refugees, families and KNU members and was razed last week in the latest attack on the camp by the DKBA. It is located near the bank of the Moei River just inside Thailand. The river marks the border between the two countries.

The DKBA was formed in 1995 after a Buddhist faction of the predominantly Christian KNU guerrillas staged a muntiny and broke away from the rebel organisation. Rebels say the DKBA is backed by Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
Since its formation, the DKBA has made dozens of raids on refugee camps inside Thailand, killing or injuring scores of people.

The KNU, one of the world's oldest rebel organisations, was formed in 1948 to fight for autonomy from Rangoon. Despite losing its headquarters after the DKBA's breakaway in 1995, the rebels have vowed to continue fighting.
The DKBA says it will keep attacking the refugees until they all return to Burma and surrender to the SLORC.
About 70,000 ethnic Karen have fled the fighting inside Burma and live in the sprawing refugee camps just inside the Thai border.
